source.title: ISC 2020 Examination: Physics Paper 1 (Theory)
source.subject: physics
source.authorityName: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
source.extractionTool: pdftotext (poppler), -enc UTF-8, raw and -layout modes; pdfplumber to check glyph size/baseline of sub/superscripts
source.notes: Genuine ISC 2020 board examination paper (Physics Paper 1, Theory, 861A) from the CISCE Archive Library bundle ISC-2020-QP1.zip; the year comes from the bundle (the paper itself prints only the code 1220-861A in its footer). No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. Cover: Maximum Marks 70, Time allowed Three hours plus 15 minutes reading time (not included in durationMinutes). The paper states 8 printed pages; the PDF has 8 pages. Section A: Question 1 (12 marks) = (A) five 1-mark MCQs [5×1] and (B) seven 1-mark short answers [7×1], stored as parts '(A)(i)'..'(B)(vii)'. Section B: Questions 2-12, 2 marks each; Section C: Questions 13-19, 3 marks each; Section D: Questions 20-22, 5 marks each. Internal-choice alternatives (a)/(b) separated by OR (Questions 2, 5, 15, 17, 20, 21, 22) share choiceGroup = the question number. Questions whose sub-parts carry no separate marks are kept together. Stacked fractions and powers set with Symbol/Cambria Math glyphs (Q1(A)(i), Q1(A)(iv), Q10, Q13, Q16) were rebuilt inline after checking glyph positions and sizes with pdfplumber; small lowered digits/letters (E₁, I₂, f₁, μᵣ, fₒ) were rebuilt as Unicode subscripts. Cambria Math italic letters (𝜋, 𝛿, 𝜃, 𝛼, 𝛽) are given as plain Greek letters. Q12 (modulation/demodulation, communication systems) is on a topic not in the current chapter list, so its chapter is null. Logic-gate and transistor parts (Q19, Q22) are mapped to the semiconductor chapter.
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

(i) Electric current flowing through it, when it is operated on a 250V supply.

(ii) State any one source of ultraviolet radiations.

(ii) Concave mirror to get a real and diminished image?

(ii) demodulation?

questions.text:
A parallel plate capacitor is charged by a battery, which is then disconnected. A dielectric slab having dielectric constant (relative permittivity) K, is now introduced between its two plates in order to occupy the space completely. State, in terms of K, its effect on the following:
(i) The capacitance of the capacitor.
(ii) The potential difference between its plates.
(iii) The energy stored in the capacitor.

questions.text: A compound microscope consists of two convex lenses having focal length of 1·5cm and 5cm. When an object is kept at a distance of 1·6cm from the objective, the final image is virtual and lies at a distance of 25cm from the eyepiece. Calculate magnifying power of the compound microscope in this set-up.

In Young’s double slit experiment, the screen is kept at a distance of 1·2m from the plane of the slits. The two slits are separated by 5mm and illuminated with monochromatic light having wavelength 600nm. Calculate:
(i) Fringe width i.e. fringe separation of the interference pattern.
(ii) Distance of 10th bright fringe from the centre of the pattern.

Draw the energy level diagram of hydrogen atom and show the transitions responsible for:
(i) absorption lines of Lyman series.
(ii) emission lines of Balmer series.

(i) State any one difference between energy band diagram of conductors and that of insulators.
(ii) Give a relation between α and β for a transistor. (Derivation is not required.)
(iii) What is the advantage of an LED bulb over the filament electric bulb?

(i) A 400Ω resistor, a 3H inductor and a 5µF capacitor are connected in series to a 220V, 50Hz ac source. Calculate the:
(1) Impedance of the circuit.
(2) Current flowing through the circuit.
(ii) Draw a labelled graph showing the variation of impedance (Z) of a series LCR circuit versus frequency ( f ) of the ac supply.

(i) When an alternating emf e = 310 sin (100πt)V is applied to a series LCR circuit, current flowing through it is i = 5 sin(100πt + π/3)A.
(1) What is the phase difference between the current and the emf?
(2) Calculate the average power consumed by the circuit.
(ii) Obtain an expression for the resonant frequency (fₒ) of a series LCR circuit.
